sentences.text: A few more required items, and then the ones a professional carries anyway.
Navigation lights and sound-signaling equipment that meet the rules you just studied.
On boats twenty-six feet and over, the oil discharge placard and the garbage placard.
If there’s an installed toilet, a Coast Guard certified marine sanitation device.
And one thing that isn’t equipment at all: a safety briefing before every trip.
Where the life jackets are, how to put one on, and what to do if something goes wrong.
It takes two minutes at the dock.
Beyond the minimum, I’d carry a registered EPIRB or personal locator beacon, a VHF with DSC, a real first aid kit, and a high-water alarm.
Extinguishers: one, two, three by length.
And four minutes on the blower.
Next time: what to do when there’s a fire anyway.
